doc.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Bernard McKinney and Claude Black's nurturing teaching
summary: Fuller says few Detroit trombonists existed, recalls McKinney, and says Claude Black taught him by playing tunes along with him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: I read somewhere that there weren’t many.
No, there was McKinney left his trombone because he couldn’t keep up.
Yeah, Bernard McKinney, he’s from the McKinney family. All his family played classical music with him. He had a pretty sound on the euphonium. He didn’t have the same sound on the trombone.
Now, did Claude actually teach you?

Yes he did. He nurtured me. He really nurtured me. He taught me how to play this song and he’d play it with me. That’s teaching you. You know, just like the medical profession, when they have the table down there in the operation and they have all the medical students sitting around checking the thing out. It was that type of thing.
